runs.text: A hundred dollars in twenty fifteen. Change it into your local money, and wait ten years. Here is what it is worth in dollars, every year. Jordan, Saudi Arabia and the UAE stay at a hundred. Their money is pegged to the dollar. Syria's pound keeps collapsing in the civil war. Turkey's lira slides every single year. Egypt devalues again and again. Lebanon's banks freeze in twenty nineteen. Then the pound falls off a cliff. Iran's official rate is frozen, so it tells us nothing. No data. The euro ends near a hundred and two. The British pound, eighty six. Which currency surprised you? Tell me in the comments. And Israel, after two years of war? The shekel. It peaks at a hundred and twenty in twenty twenty one, and ends at a hundred and twelve dollars and sixty cents.
